arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Ms. Harris argued that Section 355(f) requires judicial review of all final Board decisions.
Mr. Raynor argued that statutory text limits review to specific rights and liabilities, excluding reopening denials.
chief_justice_roberts_noted that statutory violations are not automatically constitutional violations.
Justice Alito asked if the Court could decide the case by looking only at Section 231g language.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: The dispute centers on whether federal courts can review a Railroad Retirement Board decision refusing to reopen a prior benefits determination. the sides that brought the case argue the statute mandates review of all final Board decisions. The government contends the statute limits review to specific rights and liabilities, excluding procedural reopening denials.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This case determines whether federal courts can correct errors in Railroad Retirement Board procedures. It defines the scope of judicial oversight over federal benefits agencies. It affects the ability of beneficiaries to challenge agency decisions in court.
